# Agents should consider architectural elegance

## Summary

Add an `elegance-guidelines` field to the agent schema that prompts agents to evaluate whether their approach is the most elegant solution to the problem they’re assigned.

## Current state

- Agents are defined in `.agentkit/spec/agents.yaml` with rich guidance:
  - role, responsibilities, domain-rules, conventions, anti-patterns, examples, preferred-tools
  - Issue templates already capture area, priority, severity, impact, and alternatives
- There is no explicit prompt for agents to consider architectural elegance or design simplicity when solving a problem

## Problem

- Agents can technically solve a task but choose overly complex or brittle designs
- No systematic prompt to reconsider whether a simpler, more maintainable solution exists
- Architectural drift can accumulate when agents prioritize functionality over elegance

## Proposed change

### Add an `elegance-guidelines` field to agents

Add a new optional field in `agents.yaml` under each agent:

```yaml
elegance-guidelines:
  - Prefer single-responsibility modules over utility bags
  - Choose the simplest data structure that satisfies the use case
  - Avoid premature abstraction; extract only when duplication is evident
  - Prefer standard library patterns unless a custom abstraction is clearly justified
```

### Why this fits AgentKit Forge

- It lives in the agent persona definition, where agents already look for guidance
- It can be tailored per agent (backend vs frontend vs infra)
- It mirrors existing fields like `conventions` and `anti-patterns`
- It doesn’t impose new process overhead on issue creation

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add `elegance-guidelines` as an optional field in the agent schema
- [ ] Populate initial elegance guidelines for core engineering agents (backend, frontend, infra, devops)
- [ ] Update spec-validator to accept the new field
- [ ] Regenerate issue templates and agent files to confirm compatibility
- [ ] Document the new field in the agents.yaml header comment

## Alternatives considered

- Issue-template-only approach: would be process-heavy and not visible in agent context
- Domain-rule approach: would mix architectural guidance with project policy; better to keep it agent-local

## Additional context

This change is inspired by recent code review feedback where technically correct but unnecessarily complex solutions were chosen. Making elegance an explicit part of the agent’s persona encourages self-correction before code is written.

## Files to modify

- `.agentkit/spec/agents.yaml` — add `elegance-guidelines` fields
- `.agentkit/engines/node/src/spec-validator.mjs` — accept the new field
- Update generated files via `pnpm -C .agentkit agentkit:sync`

**IMPORTANT**: Do not edit generated files directly. All spec changes must be made in `.agentkit/spec/agents.yaml` and regenerated via the sync command. Files marked "GENERATED by AgentKit Forge — DO NOT EDIT" must not be modified directly. Any engine/template changes should be submitted as a PR to the agentkit-forge repository.

---

## Resolution

**Status: Resolved** (2026-03-21)

Implemented in `feat(init): kit-based wizard with dry-run, elegance-guidelines, framework...` (PR #432, `feat/kit-domain-selection-onboarding`):

- `elegance-guidelines` field added to `agents.yaml` schema and documented in the header with examples
- Initial guidelines populated for core engineering agents (backend, frontend, infra, devops) covering single-responsibility, thin abstractions, composition patterns, and consistent naming
- `spec-validator.mjs` already allowed unknown fields — no change needed
- Sync run confirmed compatibility; no generated file breakage

The `elegance-guidelines` field is now part of every agent's persona definition, alongside existing `conventions` and `anti-patterns` fields.
